rule_0.statement: The matter skeleton's 8-component reading (4 measured chains + axial composite rank 1 + singletons 14/16/19, 0 cross-component bonds) is a measurement-SCOPE artifact, not an anatomical fact: identify_bones_v2.py loaded rank 1 separately ('axial composite handled separately') so the composite was never in any gap table, and the singletons were only ever tested against nonaxial ranks 2-25 (their committed touching_neighbors is [] against that subset alone). Measured on the committed preview meshes with the law's own metric (symmetric min vertex-to-nearest-vertex surface gap, trimesh preview vertices, cKDTree) the anatomically-jointed cross-component pairs close to the SAME touching class (gap <= 3.0 mm at 0.01 mm resolution) that already holds the 21 intra-chain bonds, because the curled infant's real anatomy folds the limbs onto the trunk.

Pre-registered expected neighbor pairs (ranks from bone_identification_v3.json / manifest centroids, sides never assigned per the committed side_rule):

Two anatomical readings admitted in advance: unfused proximal femoral epiphysis (growth-plate separation, infant) or pelvic (iliac-region) ossification center.
  P6 SINGLETON 14 (compact block; centroid [26.3, 19.8, 31.4] lies BEYOND the composite's pelvis-end bbox x-min 47.3, in the caudal wrap zone) and SINGLETON 19 (centroid [19.2, 21.7, 49.5], same zone): gap <= 3.0 mm to the composite (sacrum/caudal-base reading); alternative reading admitted in advance: displaced tarsal/carpal cluster, in which case the touching gap would sit on the hind-foot bones instead. Predict: exactly one partner set carries a <= 3.0 mm gap.
  GAP SCALE: the committed intra-chain touching edges span 0.38-2.91 mm; predicted cross-component joint gaps land in the same band; 3.0 mm is the law's own cut (JOINT_GAP_MM, the shared empirical gap valley: specimen A last touch 2.91, next pair 3.30); 8.0 mm is the hard ceiling of 'anatomical neighbor' -- any predicted pair beyond it falsifies outright.
  LOCALIZATION: each hip pair's closest approach sits at/near the femur's proximal end (pelvis-side); each shoulder pair's at/near the humeral head end (skull-side); recorded, not enforced.

Refusals stand honestly; they are never tuned away by a wider threshold.

rule_1_derivation_plan.note: No new free numbers. The metric, the cut, the resolution and the pairs all come from committed law and facts; the only new numbers this lane produces are measurements.
rule_1_derivation_plan.metric_law: gap(A,B) = min( min_{v in A} dist(v, KD(V_B)), min_{v in B} dist(v, KD(V_A)) ) on trimesh.load(preview, process=False).vertices -- identify_bones_v2.py surface_gaps() verbatim (committed origin/buffy/bone-id-v2-20260919), the metric that produced the 21 committed bonds.
rule_1_derivation_plan.cut_law: touching class <= 3.0 mm = JOINT_GAP_MM (identify_bones_v2.py), derived in v2's derived_cuts.joint_gap_mm as the ONLY shared empirical gap-valley cut across both specimens (A: 2.91/3.30, B: 2.97/3.04); sensitivity-recorded. This lane does NOT choose a threshold; it reuses the law's own cut.
rule_1_derivation_plan.resolution_law: 0.01 mm (committed gap_mm resolution) for law numbers; 0.001 mm for the secondary triangle-refined gaps; float64 throughout.
rule_1_derivation_plan.refinement_law: Secondary exact point-to-triangle refinement (both directions, Ericson closest-point) over the k nearest triangle centroids with a self-verifying radius guarantee (min exact <= dist to k-th centroid, else k doubles): reported as refined_gap_mm + closest-point pair, a lower bound that documents geometric truth. The LAW number stays the vertex metric -- the committed 21 bonds and any candidate bond are defined on THAT metric, and refined_gap_mm <= law gap always.
rule_1_derivation_plan.anatomical_reading_law: Hips and shoulders are the only physiologic joints between limb chains and the axial complex: femoral head in acetabulum, humeral head in glenoid cavity of the scapula (Hartman & Straus, The Anatomy of the Rhesus Monkey, 1933 -- macaque-specific; joints homologous across mammals). The scapula carries no separate rank in v3, consistent with its segmentation merging into the composite; the pelvis likewise (composite bbox x-min 47.3 = pelvis-end). Unfused epiphyses are separate ossification centers in juveniles (Scheuer & Black, Developmental Juvenile Osteology, 2000), so a compact block adjacent to a long-bone end may be an unfused epiphysis -- the pre-registered reading for singleton 16. Caudal vertebrae continue the column beyond the sacrum (same sources), the pre-registered reading for singletons 14/19 in the wrap zone beyond the composite's pelvis end. The curled pose folding limbs onto the trunk is the specimen's own committed CT geometry, not a literature claim.
